Forecast accuracy & variance

Commodity accuracy = max(0, 1 − Σ|consumption − forecast| / Σconsumption) × 100, using only months with both values. Zero total consumption produces no accuracy score. Overview accuracy is the equal-weight mean of available commodity scores. Positive variance means consumption exceeded forecast; negative means consumption was below forecast.

Stock cover & supply risks

Months of stock = closing stock in the selected end month ÷ average monthly consumption over up to three months ending there (within January–August). All months in that window must be present. Missing stock or zero average consumption produces no stock-cover estimate. Default planning thresholds are below 3 and above 6 months; they are editable assumptions, not programme policy. Actions need confirmation against stockouts, pipeline orders, lead times and service data before changing procurement.

Data quality & programme classification

Use one row per commodity and month, with consistent units and pack sizes in the commodity name. Dates must be January–August 2026; month names alone refer to 2026. Blank numeric cells remain missing, while zero means a reported zero. Duplicate commodity-month rows, invalid values and out-of-period dates block the import. Sheets without the required Commodity, Month and Forecast headers are skipped and reported. Explicit programme labels take precedence; recognised names are classified automatically. Other products remain Unclassified for review.
